source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Identify sentinel events, analyze causes, and make improvements to reduce recurrence","B":"Report every sentinel event to Joint Commission because reporting is mandatory","C":"Delay analysis until Joint Commission requests documentation from the organization","D":"Take no formal improvement action when the organization chooses not to report externally"}}
source_row.rationale: Joint Commission states that reporting sentinel events to Joint Commission remains voluntary. However, accredited organizations are expected to identify sentinel events, examine root causes and contributing factors, and make improvements that reduce the risk of recurrence. Choosing not to report externally does not remove the organization's internal patient-safety responsibilities.
source_row.source_detail: Reporting remains voluntary; accredited organizations are expected to identify sentinel events, examine root causes/contributing factors, and improve systems; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A sentinel event occurs at a Joint Commission-accredited hospital. A staff member believes no formal review is needed if the organization chooses not to report it to Joint Commission. Which response is accurate?
